newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK ECONOMY PUT ON MIXED PERFORMANCE IN 94-96.
newsitem.headline: GREEK ECONOMY PUT ON MIXED PERFORMANCE IN 94-96.

text.p: Greece's economic performance has
been mixed over the 1994-96 period when actual figures and
estimates are compared to projections in the revised convergence
plan to align its economy with the European Union.
Figures show that Greece has done better than forecasted in
the EU plan in terms of fiscal consolidation and GDP growth but
has fared poorly in meeting the average inflation targets.
Its debt-to-GDP ratio has fallen in 1995 compared to 1994
but it is way off the 60 percent Maastricht goal.
Faster GDP growth, a smaller general government budget
deficit, a higher primary surplus and lower interest rates on
its debt point to a lower debt-to-GDP ratio for 1996.
It should be noted that part of the improvement in the
general government budget deficit is due to previously
unrecorded revenues from changes in the social security system
enacted by the conservative administration of the New Democracy
party in 1992-93.
Economics Professor George Alogoskoufis who is likely to
become finance minister under a conservative administration told
Reuters that the general government budget deficit would end up
close to 9.0 percent of GDP in 1996.
EU plan Actual
Avg inflation 10.8% 10.9%
Budget deficit/GDP 13.2% 12.1%
GDP growth 1.1% 1.5%
EU plan Estimates EU plan Prel. estimates
Avg inflation 7.9% 9.3% 6.1% 8.3%
Budget deficit/GDP 10.7% 9.0% 7.6% 7.4%
All GDP ratios are based on the national economy ministry's
latest revision in August except for the debt-to-GDP ratio which
is based on OECD figures. The debt-to-GDP ratio is in line with
the Maastricht definition.
The average inflation figure for 1995 and 12-month T-bill
rates are final.
1996 estimates are based on national economy ministry data
which might prove to be optimistic as far as inflation and
12-month T-bill interest rates are concerned.
--Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
